title: Transportation communication systems and nepotism/fraternization - 2025 handbook
summary: 2025 handbook rules for RTEC communication systems, privacy/monitoring and prohibited electronic use, plus merit-based hiring restrictions involving relatives and handling of employee relationships.

claims.claim: RTEC communication systems are described as company property for business purposes, and employees are told they should have no expectation of privacy in information created, sent, received, accessed or stored through those systems.

evidence.page_or_section: printed page 42 - RTEC Transportation Communication Systems

claims.claim: RTEC states that use of its communication systems may be accessed, monitored and audited, and that messages may be identifiable with RTEC to recipients.

The handbook prohibits use of communication systems for harassing/disparaging or slur-based content, pornography/profanity/violent or sexually explicit content, unauthorized commercial/outside solicitation, advocacy not officially endorsed by RTEC, illegal activity, spam, hacking, pirated software/copyright infringement, unauthorized distribution of sensitive/proprietary/confidential information, unauthorized access and impersonation.
Violation of the communication-system rules may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination.

The nepotism/fraternization section states that recruiting and promotion are to be based on merit rather than relationship and says RTEC does not permit employment of relatives of current RTEC employees or Board Members under the relationship definition in the policy.

evidence.note: The full source preserves the policy's relationship list.

claims.claim: When existing employees marry or enter a relationship, the exclusion normally does not apply automatically; RTEC states it will attempt to reassign one employee to a different department and employment will end within 90 days if no reassignment is available.
The nepotism/fraternization section states that it applies to all categories of employment at RTEC Transportation.

trigger: Use of RTEC communication systems, hiring/promotion involving a relative, or an employee relationship that creates a policy issue.
steps: Use communication systems for permitted business purposes.
Do not transmit/access prohibited content or perform unauthorized system activity.
If existing employees enter a covered relationship, attempt reassignment before the stated employment consequence.
decisions: Whether a family/relationship falls within the policy definition
deadlines: If no reassignment is available after a covered existing-employee relationship arises, the handbook states employment will end within 90 days.
exceptions: The handbook distinguishes a relationship that arises between existing employees from initial employment of relatives.
controls: Reassignment step before the stated 90-day consequence for existing employees
unresolved_questions: Determine whether the undated standalone Computer Use Policy is a current supplement to or predecessor of the 2025 communication-system section.
Document who makes and records nepotism/reassignment determinations.
automation_candidates: Conflict-of-interest/nepotism review checklist for hiring and transfers.
